D000573.s: A professional society in the United States whose membership is composed of hospitals.

D001307.s: The process whereby auditory stimuli are selected, organized, and interpreted by the organism.

D001822.s: The total amount of a chemical, metal or radioactive substance present at any time after absorption in the body of man or animal.

D001857.s: Extracellular substance of bone tissue consisting of collagen fibers, ground substance, and inorganic crystalline minerals and salts.

D002294.s: A carcinoma derived from stratified squamous epithelial cells. It may also occur in sites where glandular or columnar epithelium is normally present. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

D002355.s: A thiophene-containing local anesthetic pharmacologically similar to mepivacaine.

D002405.s: Placement of an intravenous catheter in the subclavian, jugular, or other central vein.

D002661.s: Facilities which administer the delivery of mental health counseling services to children.

D002944.s: Excision of the prepuce of the penis (foreskin) or part of it.

D003068.s: The use of force or intimidation to obtain compliance.

D003082.s: Surgical resection of a portion of or the entire colon.

D003420.s: A developmental malformation of the heart characterized by a twisted but not defective atrioventicular connection. The abnormal rotation of the ventricular mass around its long axis results in the crossing of the inflow streams of the two ventricles.

e: Lysosomal Cystine Transport Protein, Defect Of
D003554.s: A metabolic disease characterized by the defective transport of cystine across the lysosomal membrane due to mutation of a membrane protein cystinosin. This results in cystine accumulation and crystallization in the cells causing widespread tissue damage.

D003932.s: A narcotic analgesic that may be habit-forming. It is a controlled substance (opium derivative) listed in the U.S. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 21 Parts 329.1, 1308.11 (1987). Sale is forbidden in the United States by Federal statute. (Merck Index, 11th ed)

D003947.s: Any diagnostic evaluation using radioactive (unstable) isotopes. This diagnosis includes many nuclear medicine procedures as well as radioimmunoassay tests.

D004195.s: Naturally-occurring or experimentally-induced animal diseases with pathological processes analogous to human diseases.

D004238.s: Inflammation of a diverticulum or diverticula.

D004568.s: Diagnosis of disease states by recording the spontaneous electrical activity of tissues or organs or by the response to stimulation of electrically excitable tissue.

D004582.s: The research and development of electrical equipment and supplies for such medical applications as diagnosis, therapy, research, anesthesia control, cardiac control, and surgery. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

D005642.s: Disorder caused by loss of endothelium of the central cornea. It is characterized by hyaline endothelial outgrowths on Descemet's membrane, epithelial blisters, reduced vision, and pain.

D007327.s: The act of blowing a powder, vapor, or gas into any body cavity for experimental, diagnostic, or therapeutic purposes.

D007352.s: Insurance providing for payment of a stipulated sum to a designated beneficiary upon death of the insured.

D007402.s: A superficial dermatitis occurring on skin surfaces in contact with each other, such as the axillae, neck creases, intergluteal fold, between the toes, etc. Obesity is a predisposing factor.

D008289.s: Any of a group of infections of fowl caused by protozoa of the genera plasmodium, Leucocytozoon, and Haemoproteus. The life cycles of these parasites and the disease produced bears strong resemblance to those observed in human malaria.

D008407.s: Granulated cells that are found in almost all tissues, most abundantly in the skin and the gastrointestinal tract. Like the basophils, mast cells contain large amounts of histamine and heparin. Unlike basophils, mast cells normally remain in the tissues and do not circulate in the blood.

D008472.s: A benzodiazepine derivative used in the treatment of anxiety. It has sedative, muscle relaxant, and anticonvulsant properties. One of its metabolites is diazepam and one of its excretion products is oxazepam.

D008498.s: The creation and maintenance of medical and vital records in multiple institutions in a manner that will facilitate the combined use of the records of identified individuals.

D009444.s: An experimental animal model for the demyelinating disease of guillaine-barre syndrome. In the most frequently used protocol, animals are injected with a peripheral nerve tissue protein homogenate.

D009750.s: A collective term for nutritional disorders resulting from poor absorption or nutritional imbalance, and metabolic disorders resulting from defects in biosynthesis (anabolism) or breakdown (catabolism) of endogenous substances.

D009905.s: The method of measuring the dispersion of an optically active molecule to determine the relative magnitude of right- or left-handed components and sometimes structural features of the molecule.

D010033.s: Inflammation of the middle ear including the auditory ossicles and the eustachian tube.

D010983.s: The preparation of platelet concentrates with the return of red cells and platelet-poor plasma to the donor.

D011012.s: Deliberate introduction of air or gas into the mediastinum as an aid to examination and diagnosis.

D012570.s: Requirements for the selection of students for admission to academic institutions.

D012927.s: Those forms of control which are exerted in less concrete and tangible ways, as through folkways, mores, conventions, and public sentiment.

D012952.s: Organizations composed of members with common interests and whose professions may be similar.

D013021.s: A state in south central Australia. Its capital is Adelaide. It was probably first visited by F. Thyssen in 1627. Later discoveries in 1802 and 1830 opened up the southern part. It became a British province in 1836 with this self-descriptive name and became a state in 1901.

D013245.s: Procedures to block or remove all or part of the genital tract for the purpose of rendering individuals sterile, incapable of reproduction. Surgical sterilization procedures are the most commonly used. There are also sterilization procedures involving chemical or physical means.

D013559.s: The relationship between two different species of organisms that are interdependent; each gains benefits from the other or a relationship between different species where both of the organisms in question benefit from the presence of the other.

D013696.s: The property of objects that determines the direction of heat flow when they are placed in direct thermal contact. The temperature is the energy of microscopic motions (vibrational and translational) of the particles of atoms.

D013991.s: Idiopathic painful nonsuppurative swellings of one or more costal cartilages, especially of the second rib. The anterior chest pain may mimic that of coronary artery disease. (Dorland, 27th ed.)

D015423.s: Refers to any inflammation of the sclera including episcleritis, a benign condition affecting only the episclera, which is generally short-lived and easily treated.

D016246.s: Lymphocytes that show specificity for autologous tumor cells. Ex vivo isolation and culturing of TIL with interleukin-2, followed by reinfusion into the patient, is one form of adoptive immunotherapy of cancer.

D016516.s: Ratio of T-lymphocytes that express the CD4 antigen to those that express the CD8 antigen. This value is commonly assessed in the diagnosis and staging of diseases affecting the immune system including hiv infections.

D016871.s: Infections with bacteria of the family pasteurellaceae.

D017533.s: A demographic parameter indicating a person's status with respect to marriage, divorce, widowhood, singleness (single person), etc.

D019283.s: A severe form of acute inflammation of the pancreas characterized by one or more areas of necrosis in the pancreas with varying degree of involvement of the surrounding tissues or organ systems. Massive pancreatic necrosis may lead to diabetes mellitus, and malabsorption.

D019706.s: Depolarization of membrane potentials at the synaptic membranes of target neurons during neurotransmission. Excitatory postsynaptic potentials can singly or in summation reach the trigger threshold for action potentials.

D020643.s: Three nuclei located beneath the dorsal surface of the most rostral part of the thalamus. The group includes the anterodorsal nucleus, anteromedial nucleus, and anteroventral nucleus. All receive connections from the mamillary body and brain fornix, and project fibers to the cingulate body.

D041743.s: The adverse or beneficial effect of medicinal herbs on the activity, metabolism, or toxicity of pharmaceuticals.

D046728.s: A condition characterized by chronic watery diarrhea of unknown origin, a normal colonoscopy but abnormal histopathology on biopsy. This syndrome was first described in 1980 by Read and associates. Subtypes include collagenous colitis and lymphocytic colitis.

D047868.s: A benign neoplasm of pneumocytes, cells of the pulmonary alveoli. Originally considered to be vascular in origin, it is now classified as an epithelial tumor with several elements, including solid cellular areas, papillary structure, sclerotic regions, and dilated blood-filled spaces resembling…

D048429.s: The quantity of volume or surface area of cells.

D049268.s: An imaging technique using compounds labelled with short-lived positron-emitting radionuclides (such as carbon-11, nitrogen-13, oxygen-15 and fluorine-18) to measure cell metabolism. It has been useful in study of soft tissues such as cancer; cardiovascular system; and brain.

D053717.s: Serious inflammation of the LUNG in patients who required the use of pulmonary ventilator. It is usually caused by bacterial cross infection in hospitals.

D054024.s: The most posterior portion of the hindbrain from which medulla oblongata is derived.

D054262.s: A process of complicated morphogenetic cell movements that reorganizes a bilayer embryo into one with three germ layers and specific orientation (dorsal/ventral; anterior/posterior). Gastrulation describes the germ layer development of a non-mammalian blastula or that of a mammalian blastocyst.

D055009.s: A degenerative spinal disease that can involve any part of the vertebra, the intervertebral disk, and the surrounding soft tissue.

D055100.s: Thin strands of transparent material, usually glass, that are used for transmitting light waves over long distances.

D055618.s: Instruments and apparatus for radiation applications and their components and associated expendables.

D055687.s: Properties, and processes of the musculoskeletal system and the nervous system or their parts.

D056325.s: Substances used to identify the location and to characterize the types of neural pathways.

D057775.s: The application of repeated, brief periods of vascular occlusion at the onset of reperfusion to reduce reperfusion injury that follows a prolonged ischemic event. The techniques are similar to ischemic preconditioning but the time of application is after the ischemic event instead of before.

D058028.s: Detailed account or statement or formal record of data resulting from empirical inquiry.

D062906.s: Catheters inserted into various locations within the heart for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes.

D063246.s: Transformative processes which occur in cells and tissues to produce differentiated plant organs.

D066245.s: Set of nerve fibers that cross the midline of the telencephalon. They include the anterior commissure; the corpus callosum; and the hippocampal commissure of the fornix.

D000067208.s: Allergic reaction to shellfish or shellfish products.

D000072956.s: Progenitor stem cells found in the testicles.

D000081002.s: Military conflict involving China and Japan 1937 - 1945.

e: CHIP Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential
ICUS Idiopathic Cytopenias of Undetermined Significance
CCUS Clonal Cytopenia of Undetermined Significance
D000082182.s: Expansion of blood cells arising from mutant hematopoietic stem cells often related to aging. Mutations on epigenetic regulator genes are common in clonal hematopoiesis and may be a risk factor for hematologic neoplasms and other cardiovascular diseases.

D000084922.s: Dietary starch and related high-molecular carbohydrate incapable of enzymatic hydrolysis in the small intestine and instead ferments in the colon, producing short-chain fatty acids by-products.

D000086502.s: Specific sequences in the viral nucleic acid that are involved in packaging the viral genome (viral genome packaging) into the virus particles.

D000092723.s: The use of a dose of electricity that causes the pores that are formed in cell membranes during electroporation to remain open long enough to trigger cell death. It is sometimes used in conjunction with electrochemotherapy.

D000094703.s: A method of comparing the cost of a program with its expected outcomes that are qualitative in nature. Cost effectiveness compares alternative ways to achieve a specific set of results.

D000099106.s: Presence of vestibular symptoms such as light-headedness, dizziness or unsteadiness associated with injuries and pathologies of the cervical vertebrae. Cervicogenic dizziness are often associated with a whiplash-type injury and neck pain.
